Exactly one scenario remains skipped: §16.3 scenario 12, Admin_ResetsTotpUser_ForcesPasswordThenTotpReenrollment, at EndToEndScenarios.cs:1936.

What Slice 15 needs to be
Spec wording: "Admin resets a TOTP-enrolled user → user password sign-in → forced password change → forced TOTP re-enrollment → lands home; passkey sign-in path also hits the pipeline."

I traced the whole path through the real code. Three findings worth recording, because two of them are latent harness bugs:

1. AccountJourneys.SignOutAsync will throw a strict-mode violation on exactly the pages this scenario must sign out from. It uses a bare page.Locator("form.sign-out-form button[type='submit']") — a strict locator. Both ChangePasswordRequired.razor and EnrollTotpRequired.razor render a sign-out form of their own beside the header's, so the locator resolves to two elements. Needs .First. This matters because /sign-in is not in ObligationsEnforcement.IsExemptPath, so a trapped principal cannot reach the sign-in page at all — sign-out is the only way out, and the harness currently can't do it.

2. The staff account needs two browser contexts, not one. passkey.js's tryAutofillPasskey() fires a conditional-mediation credentials.get() on every sign-in page load, and the virtual authenticator has automaticPresenceSimulation: true plus a resident key — so once a passkey is registered in that context, a "password sign-in" there may silently become a passkey sign-in and the test would pass for the wrong reason. So: staffDevice (with authenticator) does the passkey registration and the passkey sign-ins; staffTerminal (no authenticator) does the password walk through the pipeline.

3. One product change only — ManagePerson.razor's reset panel writes the temporary password into <p class="totp-secret">, the same password/TOTP-secret selector collision Slice 12 fixed on CreateStaff.razor. It needs class="totp-secret staff-temporary-password" so the harness isn't reading a password out of an element named for an authenticator key on one page and a real TOTP secret out of the same class on the next. Everything else the scenario needs already exists in the markup (.manage-facts groups keyed by span.manage-label, read via Slice 14's ScreenText.DeclaredAsync since that label is upcased).

Verified along the way: CreateStaffAsync sets must_change_password but not must_enroll_totp (so the voluntary /account/enroll-totp surface is needed to arrange the enrolled state); ResetCredentialsAsync sets both flags and nulls totp_secret_protected only when one was enrolled, returning ClearedAuthenticator — which the panel's status-success sentence distinguishes; recovery-code sets are 10 (RecoveryCode.CodesPerSet) and the reset deletes the old ones, so asserting the two sets are disjoint is a free, strong claim; and the pipeline's destination really is / end to end, so "lands home" is literal.

The planned files: AccountJourneys.cs (the .First fix, forced-TOTP completion, voluntary enrollment and passkey-add journeys), AdministrationJourneys.cs (reset journey + a .manage-facts reader), EndToEndScenarios.cs (scenario 12), ManagePerson.razor (the one class), plus docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md and _CHANGES.md. Files to delete: none.

Say continue and I'll write the full files and package the .tar.gz.

File	Change

_CHANGES.md	the write-up
All five pre-edit files matched the SHA-256 hashes export.sh recorded, so every byte I didn't touch is known identical to your tree. This is the last placeholder — 15 live [Fact]s, zero [Fact(Skip)].

Two things the scenario found before it could be written, both worth knowing independently of it:

SignOutAsync could not sign a trapped principal out. /sign-in isn't in IsExemptPath, so sign-out is the only route out of the pipeline — but both obligation pages render a sign-out form of their own beside the header's, and the bare Locator there resolves to two elements and throws a strict-mode violation. .First fixes it; both forms are identical in effect. Scenario 12 needs it twice.

One person needs two browsers. passkey.js fires a conditional-mediation credentials.get() on every sign-in page load, and the virtual authenticator has a resident key plus automatic presence simulation — so once a credential exists in that context, a "password sign-in" there can be answered by the authenticator before a password is typed. It would still land on the forced-change page, so the test would pass for the wrong reason. Hence a device (holds the passkey) and a terminal (no authenticator, does the password walk). The one password sign-in on the device is the first one, safe because the authenticator is still empty.

The scenario also asserts the mechanism is released, not just that it fires — without that, "the passkey path hits the pipeline" is satisfied by a middleware that blocks passkeys forever. That's why the device signs out before the terminal clears the flags: the middleware reads the cookie's claims, not the row, so a stale session couldn't distinguish a fresh cookie from ChangePasswordRequired.razor's own stale-claim guard.

Expected: dotnet test → 971 / 0 failed / 957 succeeded / 14 skipped, and MYRESTAURANT_E2E=1 → 15 passed, 0 skipped, the first fully green E2E run. One caveat in _CHANGES.md: the claude-terminal.txt in this dump predates Slice 14, so if Slice 14's own run came out differently, offset these by the same amount — this slice moves exactly one test from skipped to run.
